It emits types in memory, calls `IsWow64Process2` for its own PowerShell process, and checks the two named assembly paths. I cannot endorse the **exact-source attempt as currently enforced**, because the driver rereads the controller after checking its saved identity. Repair that binding, then review the repaired saved revision before the one guest attempt.

Findings for the integration owner, all against `21f35b693eb13f2eed4abb836da2494166a0bb16`:

1. **Source binding has a time-of-check gap.** [run_fixture.py:39](/Users/ryan/.t3/worktrees/chirality-app/t3-0721d905/app/examination/windows_platform/run_fixture.py:39) compares all six files with the commit, but [run_fixture.py:48](/Users/ryan/.t3/worktrees/chirality-app/t3-0721d905/app/examination/windows_platform/run_fixture.py:48) rereads `Controller.ps1` afterwards and hashes that later content. A change between those operations can be transported and executed while the report still records the committed hash. The guest hash proves transport integrity for the later bytes; it does not prove they were the reviewed bytes. Pass the already verified saved bytes into command construction, and bind the embedded hash to that verified content. The running driver itself also needs a controlled, unchanged invocation.

2. **The 25-second limit is a response deadline, not a strict end-to-end or guest-process deadline.** [run_fixture.py:128](/Users/ryan/.t3/worktrees/chirality-app/t3-0721d905/app/examination/windows_platform/run_fixture.py:128) starts the clock before `Popen`, but process creation itself is not timed. After expiry, [line 152](/Users/ryan/.t3/worktrees/chirality-app/t3-0721d905/app/examination/windows_platform/run_fixture.py:152) permits another five seconds for the local client to exit; exceptional cleanup can also wait. Killing that client does not establish that guest PowerShell exited. The two output streams are jointly capped at 32 KiB. Describe the deadline and any timeout as host-side, with guest completion unknown.

3. **Dormant controller: exit codes with the high bit set can throw.** [Controller.ps1:266](/Users/ryan/.t3/worktrees/chirality-app/t3-0721d905/app/examination/windows_platform/Controller.ps1:266) casts the signed result of `ReadInt32` directly to `uint32`. A process exit code such as `0xC0000005` is read as negative and PowerShell’s numeric conversion can fail instead of reporting the actual unsigned code. Preserve the four bytes as an unsigned value. This path is not invoked by the proposed bootstrap.

4. **Dormant controller: cleanup can be accepted after the stated original deadline.** [Controller.ps1:275](/Users/ryan/.t3/worktrees/chirality-app/t3-0721d905/app/examination/windows_platform/Controller.ps1:275) checks the deadline before the wait and Job accounting query, but does not check again before setting cleanup true. If those operations finish after the deadline and the watchdog has not yet run, [line 291](/Users/ryan/.t3/worktrees/chirality-app/t3-0721d905/app/examination/windows_platform/Controller.ps1:291) can signal its stop event and join it. Check the deadline after the observations and before cancelling the watchdog; treat expiry as unobserved cleanup.

The controller’s intended custody structure is otherwise visible in the source: its dedicated emitted-IL thread starts before Job setup; the Job is non-inheritable, configured for kill on close, and supplied in the creation-time Job list; creation requests neither handle inheritance nor breakaway; and original process and Job handles are retained for cleanup observation. Root death requests cleanup through last close but does **not** observe it. Initialization, emitted IL, API availability, outer-Job compatibility, watchdog behavior and cleanup remain untested on Windows. The bootstrap initializes types but does not execute or validate the watchdog lifecycle.

The [sharing-guard analysis](/Users/ryan/.t3/worktrees/chirality-app/t3-0721d905/execution/PKG-01/DEL-01-02/Design/windows_process_fixture_evidence/guarded_bootstrap_api_basis.md:6) accurately supports withholding namespace admission for the proposed pathname-based compiler route. Microsoft’s [CreateFileW documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-createfilew) excludes attribute and extended-attribute access requests from share-mode restrictions, and [MS-FSA’s reparse operation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-fsa/4aeefef8-92c3-4abc-af7a-a610caf8a165) accepts `FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES` as an alternative in its access test. Other checks and privilege requirements still apply. This establishes a gap in the proposed proof, not a demonstrated guest exploit or universal impossibility. The actual installed compiler’s opens and temporary-file behavior remain unknown.

I inspected all six requested files and both historical review summaries. HEAD matched the requested revision, the working tree was clean for the fixture files, and the required `ebf71ce713e4d71a2b32193fd360cfda3cd1dab9` is an ancestor. I made no changes and ran no guest, compiler, fixture, or host tests.
